006DP0000000003.summary: Forecast as Commit for December 8 with strong sponsorship: the VP of Data & Analytics confirmed the budget and supports the rollout. The main risk is commercial. Procurement wants 35% off to sign this quarter, which needs CFO approval under the pricing policy, while Stackwell has quoted lower. The model estimates 68%, against 75% for the stage.

risks.text: Procurement asked for 35% off list. Discounts above 30% need CFO approval before they are quoted.
Stackwell came in with a lower quote; procurement wants a three-year cost comparison.
The close date moved to December 8 because the customer's budget meeting was rescheduled.

strengths.text: Executive sponsor engaged: Mateo Brennan (VP of Data & Analytics) confirmed the business case and that the budget is approved.
Active champion (Priya Zielinski) drafted the internal ROI memo, and a mutual action plan has dated steps.

nextSteps.text: Don't quote 35% yet. Get CFO approval first, or counter with a two-year term, which allows up to 5 extra points within the approval tiers.
Send a three-year total-cost comparison against Stackwell that includes the effort to maintain definitions and access rules.
Confirm the rescheduled budget meeting date with Mateo Brennan and update the mutual action plan.

crmUpdate.nextStep: Seek CFO approval or propose 2-year term instead of 35%; send 3-yr TCO vs Stackwell; confirm budget meeting date.
crmUpdate.description: Strong exec sponsor (VP Data & Analytics), budget approved, champion active, MAP in place. Risk: 35% discount ask (needs CFO approval) and Stackwell lower quote. Close moved to Dec 8.

openQuestions: Would a two-year term meet procurement's price target?
When is the rescheduled budget meeting?

qa.a: Not without CFO approval: the policy requires it for any discount above 30%, and approval must come before the discount is quoted. A two-year term can add up to 5 points within the same tiers.
